title: RGB-D fuse — PHOTO
scale: METRIC but NOT isolated — 75.5 x 86.0 x 65.0 in (room + couch)
note: Scale is measured from LiDAR depth, but the fuse never separates the sofa from the room, so this box describes a volume containing the couch rather than the couch. Partial coverage: 1 anchor + 6 ICP merges.
caveat: Box includes the room, not just the sofa.

title: RGB-D fuse — VIDEO
scale: METRIC but NOT isolated — 47.5 x 63.25 x 83.75 in (room + couch)
note: Same fuse, video capture. Its box disagrees with the photo run by 19–28 in per axis — that spread is the measure of how much room each one swept in, and why neither is a quotable sofa size.
caveat: Box includes the room; disagrees with the photo run by 19–28 in.

title: TRELLIS — PHOTO
scale: single-axis fit — mesh is 2184 x 1215 x 1117 mm
note: Fastest, cleanest, most complete-looking, and the least measured. It was scaled so its LONGEST axis matches the RGB-D fuse's longest dimension (2184 mm); the other two axes are whatever the model invented. Geometry is invented wherever the 4 views did not see.
caveat: Only the 2184 mm long axis was fitted; the other two are invented.

title: TRELLIS — VIDEO
scale: single-axis fit — mesh is 2127 x 2070 x 1108 mm
note: Same model, views drawn from video, same single-axis scaling — here against the video fuse's 2127 mm long axis. Its shape differs from the photo run because both the views and the fuse it borrows from differ.
caveat: Only the 2127 mm long axis was fitted; the other two are invented.

title: Meshroom — PHOTO
note: 1.30M faces, 32.6k landmarks, median landmark seen by 2 cameras. The cleaner of the two unmasked photogrammetry runs — but it reconstructs the room around the sofa as well, and flat leather still drops out.

title: Meshroom — VIDEO
note: 2.22M faces, 125k landmarks, median 3 cameras per landmark. Best statistics, but it reconstructs the whole ROOM — the sofa is a smaller share and noisier.

title: KIRI-OSS — PHOTO
method: open-source reproduction of KIRI's documented pipeline
input: 31 photos (28 kept by a fixed 90% quota)
scale: METRIC, isolated — 81 x 34 x 35 in ± 1–2 in
note: BiRefNet masking + AliceVision, scaled by fitting the RGB-only camera track onto the ARKit track (RMS 30 mm, per-camera median 24 mm, worst 70 mm). The only row whose scale is solved on geometry isolated to the sofa — the RGB-D fuse measures a room, TRELLIS borrows one axis of those numbers, Meshroom stays in SfM units. Two caveats: H is a STANDING height, mesh top to the LiDAR floor plane, so ~10 in of it is the gap under a sofa whose legs the isolation removed (the mesh you can load is 25 in tall); and 76% of its surface lies within 20 mm of the LiDAR depth while only 34% of the LiDAR surface lies within 20 mm of it — locally accurate, substantially incomplete.
caveat: H is measured to the LiDAR floor — the mesh you can load here is 25 in tall.
